# LLMS — Public Overview for openOODA (Stealth Pre-Release)
File: website/llms.txt

This file is the public overview at https://openooda.org/llms.txt.
Public home: https://openooda.org • Organization: https://github.com/openOODA

## 1. Status: Stealth Mode (Private Pre-Release)

openOODA is currently in **private pre-release development (Stealth Mode)** and is not yet publicly released. Keep an eye on https://openooda.org and https://github.com/openOODA for the upcoming public launch.

## 2. What openOODA Is

openOODA is an AI-native, capability-secured, fail-closed computing stack built from first principles across eight unified layers (`L0` through `L7`).

In conventional languages and operating systems, code runs with ambient authority: any imported library or generated routine inherits the privileges of the host process. openOODA eliminates ambient authority across the entire computing stack:

- **Zero Ambient Authority**: Every process starts with no privileges. External effects (filesystem, network, IPC, devices, display) require an explicit, unforgeable capability token.
- **Compile-Time & Hardware Verification**: Capability requirements and memory bounds are verified ahead of execution by the compiler and enforced at runtime by hardware and kernel isolation boundaries.
- **Deterministic Execution**: Linear arena allocation and zero-copy message passing provide predictable latency without garbage-collection pauses.

## 3. The 8-Layer Architecture (L0–L7)

- **Root Umbrella (`@openOODA`)**: Public portal, architectural standards, and release announcements.
- **Layer 0 (`L0` — Core)**: Capability-secure systems language, self-hosting native compiler, deterministic standard library, and developer toolchain (Private Stealth).
- **Layer 1 (`L1` — Kernel)**: Capability microkernel, hardware abstraction layers, IOMMU isolation, and user-space device drivers (Private Stealth).
- **Layer 2 (`L2` — OS)**: Zero-root operating system services, capability filesystems, networking, and isolated compatibility realms (Private Stealth).
- **Layer 3 (`L3` — Tools)**: Capability-scoped userland command-line utilities and structured data pipelines (Private Stealth).
- **Layer 4 (`L4` — Desktop)**: Capability compositor, spatial window management, interactive privacy portals, and command deck UI (Private Stealth).
- **Layer 5 (`L5` — Apps)**: Native productivity, creative, communication, and developer applications (Private Stealth).
- **Layer 6 (`L6` — Cloud)**: Distributed compute grid, content-addressed storage, encrypted mesh networking, and cluster scheduling (Private Stealth).
- **Layer 7 (`L7` — Agents)**: Bounded autonomous OODA loops (Observe, Orient, Decide, Act), verification engines, and fleet governance (Private Stealth).
